correctness.rationale: The strictly upward incidence blocks are exactly the Jacobson radical. Every path in the (h−1)-st power must use consecutive levels, giving precisely the product of independently uniform adjacent rectangular blocks, while all other interval parameters supply q^(M−D) choices. For a fixed partial product of rank r, an invertible coordinate reduction gives q^((n_i−r)n_{i+1}) times the classical rank-s count for r by n_{i+1} matrices, establishing the recurrence with all boundaries. A two-rank Markov recurrence gives the exact width-two population and the fixed-field exponential asymptotic. Independent prime-field full-radical and GF(4) extension-field matrix-power enumerations agree. These finite tests corroborate rather than prove the general theorem.

value.rationale: The nilpotency index is an intrinsic invariant of elements of the Jacobson radical; knowing the exact maximal-index stratum over every prime-power field and arbitrary level widths is a natural structural enumeration, not a randomly chosen parameter slice. The recurrence replaces q^M-element brute force with a bounded rank-state computation, and refines the deepest radical power by its canonical rank. A closed width-two formula proves rare-event survival and rank-one conditional concentration for arbitrarily tall posets, providing a coherent family with an exact qualitative transition. Full lower-index orbits are not claimed.
